Bourekas

1 cup all-purpose flour

3/4 tsp salt

1/2 cup vegetable oil

1/4 cup milk

Toppings:

1 tablespoon olive oil

1 medium onion, finely chopped

1 medium carrot, finely chopped

1 large red bell pepper, finely chopped

2 cloves garlic, finely chopped

1 teaspoon fresh parsley, finely chopped

1/4 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped

Salt and pepper to taste

1/4 cup olive oil

Directions

Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). 

In a bowl, mix flour and salt. Using a pastry blender or your fingertips, cut in vegetable oil until the mixture is the size of large peas. Gradually add milk and use a fork to blend. Add more oil or milk until it comes together and forms a dough. Turn the dough out on a lightly floured surface and knead for 1 minute. Repeat with the rest of the ingredients and blend again. Shape the dough into a ball, wrap it in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 3 days.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a non-stick pan. When it starts to smell nutty, add the onions, carrots, and peppers. Cook over medium-low heat until soft, 10 to 15 minutes.

Remove from heat and stir in garlic and parsley. Add salt and pepper and stir well. Season with salt and pepper. Allow to cool.

Remove the dough from the refrigerator. Divide into 8 equal portions (they should all be the same size). Roll each portion into a ball using flour and a rolling pin or your hands. Flatten the ball slightly. Place it on a floured surface, cover with plastic wrap and wrap it in plastic wrap to firm up the dough.

Cut the dough in half. Place one half on a floured surface and spread it evenly to an approximate circle about 1/4-inch (3 mm) thick. Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the chopped herbs, olive oil and salt and pepper over the dough. Roll it into a ball again using flour and a rolling pin or your hands. Cut in half again.
Roll each portion into a circle about 1/2 inch (10 mm) thick, about 8-10 inches (20-25 cm) in diameter.
Bake in the oven for 10 minutes. Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the edges are light golden.
